main_text.l: totum oraculum non versum relinquit. Plutarchus interpretans vetusta oraculi verba ostendit, φυλὰς φυλάξαι, ὠβὰς ὠβάξαι, esse idem quod distinguere & distribuere multitudinem in partes, quas φυλὰς & ὠβὰς olim dixere; ἀγωγεῖς[?] nuncupatos esse reges: ἀγορεύειν[?] significasse, concionem habere. Principium verò & causam reipublicæ institutæ significat Deo imputari. Porrò demonstrat, concione coactâ nemini reliquorum fuisse permissum, γνώμην εἰπεῖν[?], id est, sententiam aliquam suam ad deliberandum proponere, sed quod senatus & reges proponerent, de eo iudicandi potestatem populum habuisse[?]. Postea verò cum multitudo demendo addendoque sententias propositas perverteret, & violenter detorqueret, reges collegas Polydorum & Theopompum ista rhetræ priori adscripsisse: Si quid prave populus rogasset, ab eo senatus & reges secessionem faciunto, id est, ratum id non habento, sed omnino discedunto, & populum dimittunto, velut id quod propositum, pervertentem, & transmutantem in deterius. page.notes: Greek words: φυλάξαι and ὠβάξαι were read from a small image and may carry slightly different letters; ἀγωγεῖς, ἀγορεύειν and γνώμην εἰπεῖν are doubtful. The line "habuisse" has a mark over the final e that could be a tilde or a damaged letter. The word "popu-" ends the page and continues as "lus" on the next page. The running head is "DESCRIPTIO", the page number 308 stands at the top left. Show-through and the edge of the neighbouring page at the margins were not transcribed.
